deities: Hatkeshwar (a form of Shiva, Swayambhu Shivalinga)

history.dynasty: Solanki-era origins; present carved structure dated approximately 17th century
history.period: Tradition at the site is claimed to be very old (antiquity claims of 1,800-2,200 years are traditional, not archaeologically verified)
history.summary: The ancestral and most sacred Hatkeshwar temple, standing just outside the old town walls of Vadnagar (ancient Anandapura), the ancestral homeland of the Nagar Brahmin community for whom Hatkeshwar is the kuladevata (Ishta Devata). The shrine houses a Swayambhu (self-manifested) Shivalinga said to extend deep into the earth, with exterior carvings of Ramayana/Mahabharata scenes, Navagraha, apsaras and the Samudra Manthan. The present profusely carved structure is dated to approximately the 17th century, though worship tradition at the site is described as far older - the '1,800-2,200 years' figure is traditional only. NOTE: some web sources credit a 'Nag king Hariraj Naik, 1402' - that legend is attached to the Hatkeshwar temple at Raipur, Chhattisgarh (built 1402), not Vadnagar, and is flagged here as unverified for Vadnagar. A well-known Nagar legend says Hatkeshwar cursed the community to never settle in Vadnagar, explaining why the temple stands outside the town walls. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds 'Vadnagar', which is the town; the real state is Gujarat (district Mehsana). Opening hours unverified.

name: Hatkeshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Vadnagar (ancient Anandapura) in Mehsana district is a continuously inhabited town over two thousand years old, recorded by the 7th-century Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang and now on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list. It is the ancestral home of the Nagar Brahmin community, the birthplace of Narendra Modi, and preserves medieval monuments such as the Kirti Toran, the Hatkeshwar temple and Sharmistha Lake.
